source_claims: The map x ↦ ξ(x) sends a node x=(i,j) of [λ] to the unique rim subpath with endpoints (i,λ_i) and (λ′_j,j).
ξ(x) is a removable border strip of size h(x)=a(x)+ℓ(x)+1 and height ℓ(x), and every removable border strip is obtained uniquely this way.
diagram_candidates.reason: The lemma is explicitly a bijection between two geometric features of a Young diagram, and its remarks describe sliding the hook to the rim. A labelled example would make the map and its inverse easier to follow; the proof remains fully textual.
content_to_draw_or_check: Draw a representative Young diagram [λ] and mark x=(i,j), its arm and leg, with h(x)=a(x)+ℓ(x)+1.
Highlight ξ(x) along the rim from P=(i,λ_i) to Q=(λ′_j,j); distinguish its horizontal and vertical portions corresponding to the arm and leg.
Indicate that removing ξ(x) leaves a Young diagram, label |ξ(x)|=h(x) and height ℓ(x), and show the inverse recovering x from row(P) and column(Q).
